name: Sprigling
vellumEntry: It plants both feet and refuses to be moved. Hearthmere children use them to hold gates shut.

design.silhouette: squat four-legged bud with a heavy leaf collar

name: Bramblehusk
vellumEntry: The husk on its back is last season's growth, kept deliberately. It never sheds anything it can still use.

design.silhouette: hunched quadruped under a woven thorn shell

name: Thornmarch
vellumEntry: Old ones root in place for a season and come back up as part of the wall. Farmers build around them.

design.silhouette: broad-shouldered walker plated in mossed slabs

name: Cinderpaw
vellumEntry: It sleeps in cold ash and wakes up warm. Nobody has satisfactorily explained where the heat comes from.

design.silhouette: lean short-legged cub with an oversized tufted tail

name: Blazelynx
vellumEntry: Runs the ridgelines at dusk. You see the tail-light long before you see the animal.

design.silhouette: long-limbed cat, high shoulders, mane of ember tufts

name: Volcatrix
vellumEntry: It fights standing up, which no other cat in Caelora does. The stance is learned, not born.

design.silhouette: upright bipedal cat, braced stance, banded forearms

name: Rilltail
vellumEntry: It taps the water surface in patterns. Sorrell is convinced this is counting. Nobody can say what it is counting.

design.silhouette: flat-headed otterish shape with a broad paddle tail

name: Brookmaw
vellumEntry: Holds station against a current all day without visible effort, then moves faster than anything its size has any right to.

design.silhouette: heavy-shouldered swimmer, fluked tail, wide jaw

name: Maelstrix
vellumEntry: Old sailors will not name it out loud on the water. They say it answers, and that answering is the problem.

design.silhouette: long coiling swimmer with a crowned brow and trailing fins

name: Nibbet
vellumEntry: Every household in Caelora has a story about one. Most of the stories end with a missing loaf.

design.silhouette: small round rodent, long ears, ring-marked tail

name: Burrowen
vellumEntry: Digs a tunnel network under a field in one night. The Kellowmere quarry hires them and pretends it does not.

design.silhouette: broad digging rodent with shovel forepaws

name: Pipwing
vellumEntry: The first thing to leave before weather turns. Hearthmere farmers watch the pipwings, not the sky.

design.silhouette: small round bird, oversized head, short tail

name: Kestrelle
vellumEntry: Holds position in a headwind without moving a feather. It is showing off, and it knows it.

design.silhouette: falcon build, swept wings, banded chest

name: Galecrest
vellumEntry: Flies into the front instead of away from it. The crest sparks when the pressure drops.

design.silhouette: large raptor with a forked tail and a raised crest

name: Nettlebug
vellumEntry: Eats only stinging plants and becomes, predictably, unpleasant to handle.

design.silhouette: segmented grub with raised bristle ridges

name: Spinnet
vellumEntry: Spends four days building and one minute using. It considers this a fair trade.

design.silhouette: eight-legged spinner, high abdomen, silk spools at the hip

name: Weaverjaw
vellumEntry: It does not chase. In sixty recorded encounters, not once has it needed to.

design.silhouette: heavy-bodied spinner with armoured jaw plates

name: Tuftail
vellumEntry: Follows walkers for a mile and a half, then loses interest exactly at the parish boundary.

design.silhouette: small grazing quadruped, thick neck ruff

name: Bristlebuck
vellumEntry: Puts itself between a herd and whatever is coming. It has never once been asked to.

design.silhouette: stag-like grazer with a bristled mantle and low horns

name: Pebblet
vellumEntry: Indistinguishable from a rock until it is not. Kellowmere quarry hands kick everything twice.

design.silhouette: rounded boulder with stubby limbs and a seam of quartz

name: Cairnling
vellumEntry: Stacks itself in the shape of a waymarker and stands at crossroads. Travellers have been following them for centuries. Nobody knows where they lead.

design.silhouette: stacked slab figure, uneven shoulders, moss at the joints

name: Menhir
vellumEntry: There are nineteen on the Skyreach cliffs. There were eighteen last spring. Nobody saw it arrive.

design.silhouette: tall monolith with ore veins and a carved face

name: Fizzlet
vellumEntry: Sticks to metal fences and refuses to be removed politely.

design.silhouette: small bristling ball with two trailing filaments

name: Voltwick
vellumEntry: Emberfall pays a bounty for every one removed from the substation. The bounty has never been reduced.

design.silhouette: lean upright creature with a filament crest and forked tail

name: Rillfry
vellumEntry: Travels in counts of exactly seven. Split the shoal and both halves stop moving until it is seven again.

design.silhouette: slim darting fish with a split tail

name: Currentail
vellumEntry: Swims upstream through the Turning while everything else swims with it. Nobody has established why.

design.silhouette: streamlined swimmer with long trailing tail ribbons

name: Sootmoth
vellumEntry: Lays its eggs in still-warm hearths. Householders in Emberfall have simply given up.

design.silhouette: broad-winged moth with ember-lit wing edges

name: Chalkid
vellumEntry: Leaves a white smear on anything it touches. Quarry children use them to mark tunnels and then cannot explain the extra marks.

design.silhouette: rounded chalk lump with blunt limbs and a banded seam

name: Chalkmar
vellumEntry: Grows a shell of quarried slate over the soft chalk beneath. Nobody has ever seen one shed, and nobody has ever found a shed one.

design.silhouette: broad slab-plated walker with a chalk-white underbody

name: Mossback
vellumEntry: Moves roughly two metres a day. Surveyors mark them on charts as landmarks and have had to redraw the charts twice.

design.silhouette: low mossed boulder with a slow-blinking eye and stubby legs

name: Slatewing
vellumEntry: Roosts flat against a quarry wall and is indistinguishable from the wall until the wall leaves.

design.silhouette: angular flat-winged bird with slate plating along the back

name: Craglide
vellumEntry: Dives without a single wingbeat. The quarry calls the sound it makes on the way down "the whistle", and they stop working when they hear it.

design.silhouette: large raptor with slab-plated wings and a hooked stone beak

name: Emberbore
vellumEntry: Bores through rock by heating it until it gives up. The tunnels it leaves are perfectly round and slightly warm for a week.

design.silhouette: squat armoured digger with a glowing drill-snout

name: Lantric
vellumEntry: Hangs itself on a hook and burns steady for eleven hours. Quarry crews insist this is a coincidence and hang it up anyway.

design.silhouette: hanging iron lantern with a filament core and two hook arms

name: Frostnip
vellumEntry: Sleeps on the lake shore where the water refuses to freeze, which is the only warm place it can find and the only place it does not want to be.

design.silhouette: small frost-furred canine with icicle whiskers

name: Rimehound
vellumEntry: Runs the lake ice in packs of three. There is always a fourth set of tracks and there has never been a fourth hound.

design.silhouette: long-legged hound with a frost mane and trailing breath

name: Deeplum
vellumEntry: A single pale light, forty metres down, that has not moved in the eleven years the lake has been surveyed.

design.silhouette: trailing deep-water form with one hanging lure light

name: Tallowmoth
vellumEntry: Drawn to any steady light. Quarry crews carry a spare lamp purely to send somewhere else.

design.silhouette: pale broad-winged moth with luminous wing panels

name: Gravelet
vellumEntry: Lives in the waste rock and eats what the quarry throws away, which is most of it.

design.silhouette: scruffy digger caked in loose grit, oversized foreclaws

name: Shalefin
vellumEntry: Lies under two centimetres of water on the flats and is invisible until you tread on one. Then it is extremely visible.

design.silhouette: flat bottom-dwelling fish with a gritted upper hide

name: Tidewrack
vellumEntry: Carries a hide of cemented shingle. Brackwater dredges the channel twice a year and finds the shingle gone every time.

design.silhouette: heavy shingle-plated swimmer with a blunt ramming head

name: Pinchel
vellumEntry: Works the tideline for whatever the sea has given up on. Will fight anything for a shell it does not need.

design.silhouette: squat armoured crab with one oversized claw

name: Clatterclaw
vellumEntry: The sound of a colony working the flats at night carries a mile inland. Brackwater has stopped finding it unsettling.

design.silhouette: broad reef crab with paired shearing claws

name: Gullswift
vellumEntry: Hits the water at forty knots and comes up with something every time. Nobody has photographed a miss.

design.silhouette: long-winged seabird with a dagger bill and forked tail

name: Bladderwrack
vellumEntry: Anchors to one rock and stays there for its whole life. Prise one loose and it will find the same rock again.

design.silhouette: draped kelp column with float bladders and a holdfast base

name: Silthopper
vellumEntry: Crosses two hundred metres of open mud in under a minute and has never once been seen to walk.

design.silhouette: long-legged mud insect built for launching

name: Brinewisp
vellumEntry: Appears over the channel on flat nights. Brackwater lost eleven boats to them in one generation and then stopped following them.

design.silhouette: drifting hooded light with a trailing brine veil

name: Anchorling
vellumEntry: Every one of them is shaped like a working anchor. Brackwater has never lost an anchor it could not account for.

design.silhouette: iron anchor form with barnacled flukes and a single eye
